lesson.text: Quick memory: when do you use the recovery position? (Not responding, but breathing normally.) Today: hands-only CPR, and help for choking.
Check: tap the shoulders and ask loudly, are you all right? Then look, listen and feel for normal breathing, for no more than 10 seconds.
Not responding and not breathing normally: call {number} on speaker, and ask someone to fetch a defibrillator (an AED).
CPR: the heel of one hand in the middle of the chest, the other on top, arms straight. Push hard and fast, 100 to 120 times a minute, and let the chest come back up.
An AED talks you through every step: switch it on and do what it says. Keep pushing until help comes, and swap helpers about every 2 minutes.
Choking: if they can cough, tell them to keep coughing. If not: up to 5 back blows, then up to 5 tummy thrusts. If it doesn't clear, call {number}.
Try it in the world: open the practice room and push to the beat on Max, the training dummy. This is practice: a real first aid course teaches more.

exercises.prompt: How fast do you push in CPR?
exercises.explain: 100 to 120 a minute: hard and fast.

exercises.prompt: Where do your hands go in CPR?
exercises.hint: Over the heart, in the centre.
exercises.explain: The heel of one hand in the middle of the chest, the other hand on top.

exercises.prompt: An AED tells you what to do, step by step.
exercises.explain: True: switch it on and it talks you through every step.

exercises.prompt: Someone choking who can cough should keep coughing.
exercises.hint: Coughing is the body's own way.
exercises.explain: True: while they can cough, coughing works best.

items: check for a response and breathing
exercises.explain: Check for a response and breathing, call {number} on speaker, then push.

exercises.prompt: How many back blows do you give before the tummy thrusts?
exercises.hint: The same number as the tummy thrusts.
exercises.explain: Up to 5 back blows, then up to 5 tummy thrusts.

exercises.prompt: How long do you check for normal breathing?
exercises.explain: Look, listen and feel for no more than 10 seconds.

exercises.prompt: In CPR, let the chest come back up after each push.
exercises.hint: The heart fills up again between pushes.
exercises.explain: True: push down, then let the chest come all the way back up.

exercises.prompt: Someone is not responding but is breathing normally. CPR or the recovery position?
exercises.hint: CPR is for someone who is not breathing normally.
exercises.explain: Breathing normally: the recovery position, and call {number}.

exercises.prompt: After 2 minutes of CPR you are tired, and a friend is there. What do you do?
exercises.hint: Pushing is hard work for one person.
exercises.explain: Swap about every 2 minutes, with as little stopping as you can.

exercises.prompt: At 110 pushes a minute, how many pushes in 2 minutes?

exercises.explain: Can cough: keep coughing. Can't: back blows, then tummy thrusts.
